title: Solid-Tumour Drivers: EGFR, ALK, RAS and BRAF V600E
summary: Place EGFR, RAS and BRAF on one signalling chain, match lung drivers (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, RET) to their inhibitors, and learn why colorectal cancer needs extended RAS testing before EGFR antibodies and why BRAF assays must cover more than V600E.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 78 Hit 3 (EGFR activating mutations, ALK/ROS1/RET, KRAS in colorectal cancer), Hit 5 (BRAF V600E across melanoma, papillary thyroid and colorectal cancer) and Exam Trap 2 (KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer and EGFR antibodies). Checked against the 2017 ASCP/CAP/AMP/ASCO colorectal biomarker guideline (Sepulveda 2017), three open NSCLC reviews (Chevallier 2021, Majeed 2021, König 2021), Cheng 2018 (BRAF testing in melanoma), Kanat 2020 (BRAF-mutant colorectal cancer), Crispo 2019 and the TCGA papillary thyroid study (2014; read via a page-fetch tool, first part of the page only). Qualifications taught: extended RAS (KRAS and NRAS exons 2–4) rather than KRAS alone; ALK is about 3–7% (reviewer ≈7% is the upper end); melanoma BRAF is about 40–60% in Cheng 2018 (reviewer 66%, inside Crispo’s wider 30–70%) and papillary thyroid 62% in TCGA (reviewer ≈45%); in colorectal cancer BRAF V600E is targeted in combination with an EGFR antibody, not like melanoma. Not taught (not verified): the reviewer’s split of exon 19 deletions >50% vs L858R ≈40%; the Number Vault lung turnaround time. The lung CAP/IASLC/AMP 2018 guideline was not accessible as open full text and was not read.

objectives: Place EGFR, RAS, BRAF and MEK on the MAPK signalling chain and explain why a block above a stuck link fails.

Match lung adenocarcinoma drivers (EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R, ALK, ROS1, RET) to their inhibitor classes and name T790M as the commonest cause of resistance to first- and second-generation EGFR TKIs.
State the extended RAS testing required before EGFR antibodies in colorectal cancer, and why a V600E-only BRAF assay can miss V600K.

scenes.title: Three tumours, three reports
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three molecular reports. (1) Lung adenocarcinoma in a never-smoker: EGFR exon 19 deletion detected. (2) Metastatic colorectal cancer: “KRAS exon 2 wild-type”; the oncologist plans an EGFR antibody. (3) Metastatic melanoma: a real-time PCR assay that detects only BRAF V600E is negative. Question token: “Which report is complete?”

cues.text: Three molecular reports arrive. A never-smoker’s lung adenocarcinoma has an EGFR exon nineteen deletion.
A metastatic colon cancer is reported as KRAS exon two wild-type, and an EGFR antibody is planned. A melanoma is negative on an assay that detects only BRAF V600E.
Which of these reports is enough to choose a drug?

scenes.title: One signalling chain
scenes.altText: Schematic chain of five tokens left to right: EGFR (receptor) → RAS → RAF (BRAF) → MEK → ERK, labelled “MAPK signalling”. Three cards below: EGFR — exon 19 deletions + exon 21 L858R ≈ 90% of activating EGFR mutations, switch the receptor on without ligand; KRAS — below EGFR, when stuck on an upstream EGFR block cannot switch it off; BRAF V600E — activated kinase, BRAF inhibitors (vemurafenib, dabrafenib) and MEK inhibitors (trametinib, cobimetinib).

cues.text: EGFR is a receptor on the cell surface. When it is switched on, it signals down the RAS, RAF, MEK, ERK cascade, also called MAPK signalling, which drives cell division.

A driver alteration leaves one link switched on without a signal. In lung cancer, exon nineteen deletions and the exon twenty-one L858R mutation make up about ninety percent of activating EGFR mutations.
KRAS sits below EGFR. When mutant KRAS is stuck on, blocking the receptor above it cannot switch the signal off.
BRAF sits below RAS. The V600E mutation activates the BRAF kinase. Vemurafenib and dabrafenib inhibit mutant BRAF, and trametinib and cobimetinib block MEK just downstream.

scenes.title: Lung: which driver, which drug
scenes.altText: Four cards. EGFR: ≈20% of lung adenocarcinomas overall; ≈12–15% in white and ≈47–64% in East Asian patients (one review’s table); TKIs erlotinib, gefitinib, afatinib, dacomitinib, osimertinib. Resistance: exon 20 T790M is the commonest cause (≈50–60%) of resistance to first/second-generation TKIs; osimertinib inhibits it. ALK: rearrangements (usually EML4-ALK) in ≈3–7% of NSCLC, more often younger never/light smokers; crizotinib, alectinib, lorlatinib. ROS1 ≈1–2% and RET ≈1–2% of lung adenocarcinomas (ROS1: crizotinib, entrectinib · RET: selpercatinib, pralsetinib).

cues.text: In lung adenocarcinoma, EGFR driver mutations are found in about one in five patients overall, but the rate depends on ancestry: about twelve to fifteen percent in white patients and forty-seven to sixty-four percent in East Asian patients in one review’s table.

EGFR inhibitors include erlotinib, gefitinib, afatinib, dacomitinib and osimertinib. The exon twenty T790M mutation is the commonest cause of resistance to first- and second-generation drugs, and osimertinib inhibits it.

ALK rearrangements, usually EML4-ALK, are found in about three to seven percent of non-small cell lung cancers, more often in younger never- or light-smokers. ALK inhibitors include crizotinib, alectinib and lorlatinib.
ROS1 and RET rearrangements are each found in about one to two percent of lung adenocarcinomas. ROS1 responds to crizotinib or entrectinib, and RET fusions to selpercatinib or pralsetinib.

scenes.title: Colon and melanoma: read the whole report
scenes.altText: Left card (2017 ASCP/CAP/AMP/ASCO colorectal guideline): cetuximab and panitumumab bind EGFR; they benefit KRAS wild-type but not KRAS-mutant tumours; KRAS mutated in ≈39–42% (one cited study); patients considered for anti-EGFR therapy must have extended RAS testing — KRAS and NRAS exons 2 (codons 12, 13), 3 (59, 61) and 4 (117, 146). Right card, BRAF across tumours: melanoma ≈40–60% BRAF-mutant (V600E most common, V600K ≈8–20%); papillary thyroid 61.7% BRAF-mutant, mostly V600E (TCGA, 402 tumours); colorectal ≈8% advanced, ≈14% stage II–III. Hook answers card: (1) EGFR TKI candidate; (2) extended RAS first; (3) V600E-only assay can miss V600K — use broader testing.

cues.text: In colorectal cancer, cetuximab and panitumumab bind EGFR. They improved survival in KRAS wild-type tumours but not in KRAS-mutant ones. In one study cited by the guideline, about forty percent of tumours carried a KRAS mutation.
So the 2017 colorectal guideline says patients considered for these antibodies must have extended RAS testing: KRAS and NRAS, exons two, three and four. Exon two alone is incomplete.

BRAF V600E crosses tumour types. About forty to sixty percent of melanomas carry a BRAF mutation, most often V600E, and V600K makes up about eight to twenty percent of the BRAF mutations. In the cancer genome atlas thyroid study, sixty-two percent of papillary carcinomas were BRAF-mutant, and in colorectal cancer it is about eight to fourteen percent.
Back to the hook. The lung tumour is an EGFR-inhibitor candidate. The colon tumour needs extended RAS testing first. And a V600E-only assay can miss V600K, so the melanoma needs broader BRAF testing.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “KRAS-mutant colon cancer responds to cetuximab” (✓ mutant RAS signals below the blocked receptor — no benefit); “KRAS exon 2 wild-type means RAS wild-type” (✓ extended RAS: KRAS and NRAS exons 2, 3, 4); “BRAF V600E colon cancer is treated like melanoma” (✓ in colon cancer a BRAF inhibitor alone lets EGFR reactivate MAPK signalling; BEACON combined encorafenib with cetuximab).

cues.text: Trap one: KRAS-mutant colon cancer responds to cetuximab. No: mutant RAS signals below the blocked receptor, so the antibody gives no benefit.
Trap two: KRAS exon two wild-type means RAS wild-type. No: test KRAS and NRAS across exons two, three and four.
Trap three: BRAF V600E colon cancer is treated like melanoma. No: in colon cancer a BRAF inhibitor alone lets EGFR switch the pathway back on, so the BEACON trial combined encorafenib with cetuximab.

lines: ✓ Mutant RAS signals below the block

scenes.title: Block at or below the jam
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Block at or below the jam.” The signalling chain is a row of switches; a drug helps only if it blocks the stuck switch or one below it. Tokens: EGFR jammed → EGFR inhibitor · RAS jammed → EGFR antibody useless · BRAF jammed → BRAF + MEK inhibitors. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: block at or below the jam. If EGFR is stuck on, an EGFR inhibitor works. If RAS is stuck on, an EGFR antibody above it is useless. If BRAF is stuck on, block BRAF and MEK.

Where it breaks: pathways branch and feed back, so in colon cancer a BRAF block alone reactivates EGFR signalling. Resistance mutations such as T790M appear under treatment. And ALK, ROS1 and RET fusions are other kinases that feed this chain, each with its own inhibitor.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Lung: EGFR ex19 del/L858R → EGFR TKI · ALK, ROS1, RET → own inhibitors”, “Colon: extended RAS before EGFR antibodies · BRAF: assay must cover more than V600E”.

cues.text: Match each driver to its own drug, test extended RAS before any EGFR antibody in colorectal cancer, and use a BRAF assay that covers more than V600E, because a drug helps only when it blocks the link that is stuck on.

props.label: Lung: EGFR ex19 del / L858R → TKI · ALK, ROS1, RET → own drugs
Colon: extended RAS before EGFR antibody · BRAF: beyond V600E

explanation.what: Plain language: some cancers grow because one switch in a growth-signal chain is stuck on. Drugs that block that switch, or a switch below it, can work; drugs that block a switch above it cannot. Scientific terms: epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), exon 19 deletion, L858R, T790M, RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK (MAPK) cascade, extended RAS testing (KRAS/NRAS exons 2–4), anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody (cetuximab, panitumumab), BRAF V600E/V600K, ALK, ROS1 and RET fusions.
explanation.why: Mutant KRAS or NRAS keeps signalling below the receptor, so blocking EGFR with an antibody gives no benefit; testing only KRAS exon 2 misses other RAS mutations. In colon cancer, BRAF inhibition alone removes ERK-to-EGFR negative feedback and reactivates the pathway, so BRAF is combined with an EGFR antibody.
explanation.measure: Lung: EGFR exon 19 deletions + L858R ≈ 90% of activating EGFR mutations; EGFR drivers ≈ 20% of adenocarcinomas (≈ 12–15% white, ≈ 47–64% East Asian in one table); T790M ≈ 50–60% of resistance to first/second-generation TKIs; ALK ≈ 3–7%; ROS1 ≈ 1–2%; RET ≈ 1–2%. Colorectal: KRAS mutant ≈ 39–42%; extended RAS = KRAS and NRAS codons 12/13 (exon 2), 59/61 (exon 3), 117/146 (exon 4); BRAF ≈ 8% advanced, ≈ 14% stage II–III, V600E > 90% of BRAF mutations. Melanoma: ≈ 40–60% BRAF-mutant, V600K ≈ 8–20%. Papillary thyroid: 61.7% BRAF-mutant, mostly V600E (TCGA).
explanation.differs: EGFR TKI (lung, mutant receptor) vs EGFR antibody (colon, needs RAS wild-type); KRAS exon 2 only vs extended RAS; BRAF V600E in melanoma (BRAF + MEK inhibitors) vs colon (BRAF inhibitor combined with EGFR antibody; BRAF testing also used for prognosis and Lynch triage); V600E-only assay vs broader V600 assay.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: the EGFR mutations that predict TKI response, the drug for T790M, why KRAS/NRAS-mutant colon cancer is excluded from cetuximab or panitumumab, and which lung fusions have their own inhibitors.

comparisons.title: BRAF V600E in melanoma vs colorectal cancer
comparisons.distinguisher: EGFR feedback makes a BRAF block alone weak in colon cancer.

mnemonic.text: Block at or below the jam: EGFR jammed → EGFR inhibitor; RAS jammed → an EGFR antibody above it is useless; BRAF jammed → block BRAF and MEK.
mnemonic.explanation: Places each drug relative to the stuck link in the RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK chain.
mnemonic.limitation: Pathways branch and feed back (colon BRAF block reactivates EGFR, so it is combined with an EGFR antibody); resistance mutations such as T790M arise on treatment; ALK, ROS1 and RET fusions are other kinases that also feed RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK signalling, so each needs its own inhibitor.

analogyLimitations: The signalling chain is schematic; real pathways branch (for example PI3K/AKT).
Frequencies vary by population, stage and assay; the numbers are from the cited reviews.
takeaway: Match each driver to its own drug, test extended RAS before any EGFR antibody in colorectal cancer, and use a BRAF assay that covers more than V600E, because a drug helps only when it blocks the link that is stuck on.

questions.stem: A metastatic colorectal cancer is reported as “KRAS exon 2 wild-type”, and panitumumab is being considered. Under the 2017 colorectal biomarker guideline, what is needed first?

options.text: Extended RAS testing: KRAS and NRAS exons 2, 3 and 4
options.rationale: Correct. Patients considered for anti-EGFR therapy must receive RAS testing covering KRAS and NRAS codons 12/13, 59/61 and 117/146.
Incorrect. KRAS exon 2 alone misses KRAS exon 3/4 and NRAS mutations, which also predict lack of benefit.

options.text: BRAF V600 testing to predict anti-EGFR response
options.rationale: Incorrect. The guideline found insufficient evidence to use BRAF V600 as a predictive marker for anti-EGFR response; it recommends BRAF testing for prognosis and Lynch evaluation.

options.text: PIK3CA mutation analysis to select therapy
options.rationale: Incorrect. The guideline found insufficient evidence to recommend PIK3CA analysis for therapy selection outside a clinical trial.

questions.stem: Which pair of EGFR alterations together accounts for about 90% of activating EGFR mutations in non-small cell lung cancer?

options.rationale: Correct. These two make up about 90% of activating EGFR mutations and predict response to EGFR TKIs.
Incorrect. T790M is rarely present before treatment; it is the commonest cause of acquired resistance to first- and second-generation TKIs.
Incorrect. These are rearrangements of other genes (ALK, ROS1), each with its own inhibitors.
Incorrect. These are KRAS mutations, not EGFR mutations.

questions.stem: A metastatic melanoma is negative on a real-time PCR assay that detects only BRAF V600E. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The tumour may still carry V600K, so a broader BRAF V600 assay is needed
options.rationale: Correct. V600K is about 8–20% of BRAF-mutant melanomas, and some assays detect only V600E.

options.text: The result rules out any BRAF V600 mutation
options.rationale: Incorrect. A V600E-only assay cannot detect V600K or other V600 variants.

options.text: BRAF mutations are rare in melanoma, so no further testing is needed
options.rationale: Incorrect. About 40–60% of melanomas carry a BRAF mutation.

options.text: VE1 immunohistochemistry will detect V600K instead
options.rationale: Incorrect. The VE1 antibody is specific for V600E.

claims.text: EGFR signals through the RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK (MAPK) cascade; KRAS acts downstream of EGFR; MEK is downstream of BRAF.
Exon 19 deletions + L858R ≈90% of activating EGFR mutations; EGFR drivers ≈20% of adenocarcinomas, varying by ancestry; EGFR TKIs; T790M as main resistance mutation, osimertinib.

ALK ≈3–7% of NSCLC (younger never/light smokers; crizotinib, alectinib, lorlatinib); ROS1 ≈1–2% and RET ≈1–2% of lung adenocarcinomas (ROS1: crizotinib, entrectinib; RET: selpercatinib, pralsetinib); these fusion kinases feed MAPK signalling.
Anti-EGFR antibodies benefit RAS wild-type colorectal cancer only; extended RAS testing (KRAS and NRAS exons 2–4) required; KRAS ≈39–42%; BRAF and PIK3CA not recommended as predictive markers.
BRAF ≈8% advanced / ≈14% stage II–III CRC; BRAF testing for prognosis and Lynch triage; BRAF inhibitor alone triggers EGFR feedback; BEACON combined encorafenib with cetuximab.
Melanoma ≈40–60% BRAF-mutant, V600E most common, V600K ≈8–20%; BRAF and MEK inhibitors; V600E-only assays; VE1 specific for V600E.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma 61.7% BRAF-mutant, mostly V600E (TCGA); range 36–83% across studies.
Reviewer split: exon 19 deletions >50% and L858R ≈40% of EGFR mutations.
claims.note: Not found in the sources read; not taught.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 78 Hit 3 and Exam Trap 2 name only KRAS as the marker of EGFR-antibody resistance in colorectal cancer. The 2017 ASCP/CAP/AMP/ASCO guideline (Sepulveda 2017) requires extended RAS testing (KRAS and NRAS exons 2, 3 and 4) for patients considered for anti-EGFR therapy (register flag rv-ch78-extended-ras).

Ch. 78 Hit 3 gives ALK ≈7% of lung cancer. Open reviews give 3–7% (Majeed 2021), about 5% of advanced NSCLC (Chevallier 2021) and 2–8% (König 2021); 7% is the upper end, and Majeed’s Table 1 lists 7% only for Caucasian patients (register flag rv-ch78-alk-share).

Ch. 78 Hit 5 and the Number Vault give BRAF in 66% of melanomas (80% of those V600E) and BRAF V600E in ≈45% of papillary thyroid cancers. Cheng 2018 gives about 40–60% of melanomas (about half of advanced melanomas), with V600E 84.6% of BRAF-mutant cases in its table; TCGA 2014 found BRAF mutations, mostly V600E, in 61.7% of 402 papillary thyroid carcinomas. Crispo 2019 cites wide ranges (melanoma 30–70%, papillary thyroid 36–83%) that contain both reviewer figures, so the reviewer point estimates are not wrong outright but differ from the main sources taught (register flag rv-ch78-braf-frequencies).

Ch. 78 Hit 5 lists colorectal cancer alongside melanoma as BRAF V600E-targetable. In colorectal cancer, BRAF inhibition alone is limited by EGFR feedback reactivation, and the BEACON regimen combines encorafenib with cetuximab in second/third line (Kanat 2020); the 2017 guideline recommends BRAF testing for prognosis and Lynch triage (Sepulveda 2017) (register flag rv-ch78-crc-braf-combination).

morphology.note: No micrographs; signalling chain and reports shown as tokens and cards.

verification.notes: 7 factual claims checked against Sepulveda 2017, Chevallier 2021, Majeed 2021, König 2021, Kanat 2020, Cheng 2018, Crispo 2019 and TCGA 2014 (read via a page-fetch tool); 1 reviewer claim (exon 19 vs L858R split) pending and not taught. The CAP/IASLC/AMP 2018 lung guideline was not read. No human expert has reviewed this lesson.
